response: Chronic functional somatic symptoms do not appear to represent a single syndrome. Patients with these symptoms exhibit a great diversity of functional somatic symptoms, and their symptoms do not cluster into well-defined distinct syndromes. Instead, they often experience a wide range of symptoms, and their use of somatic and psychotropic drugs, referrals, and psychiatric morbidity rates are higher than those of controls. Therefore, it is recommended that patients with chronic functional somatic symptoms not be classified into medical subspecialty syndromes, as this may not accurately reflect the complexity of their symptoms.
